# deep-modules — Rules projection

## dependencies

deep-modules/MD-01  No module cycles. Sibling modules under one parent never use each other, directly or through other siblings, in a circle. A module using its own children, or a child using its ancestors, is not a cycle; crates and packages are already ordered by the build tool.

deep-modules/MD-02  No tangles. Types or functions that use each other in a circle live in one module, and there are at most seven of them. A loop that crosses modules, or one too big to hold in mind, is broken by moving the shared decision up a layer.

## interfaces

deep-modules/MD-03  No field leaks. When a type keeps any field to itself and has its own methods over its fields, code outside the type and its tangle does not write, mutably borrow, index, or call mutating methods on those fields, directly or through getters and setters. Copying a value out, or a read-only query such as `len` or `is_empty`, is not a leak.

deep-modules/MD-04  No shallow modules. A crate, package, or module with child modules that shows outside callers more than seven functions must hide more functions than it shows, and no list a reader must learn (its exported types, or one type's functions) runs longer than seven.

## layout

deep-modules/MD-05  No wide directories. A directory holds at most fifteen entries counting source files and subdirectories that contain source files.
            check: scripts/check-structure --max-entries 15

deep-modules/MD-06  No long files. A source file has at most 2,000 lines, counting blank lines, comments and test code.
            check: scripts/check-structure --max-lines 2000

## repair

deep-modules/MD-07  Fix structure from first principles. A finding is resolved by deciding which layer each piece belongs to and what the narrow interface is, not by moving, renaming, re-exporting or wrapping code until a check stops reporting it. Each fix shows a before-and-after picture of the structure.

deep-modules/MD-08  Ratchet existing debt. A codebase adopting this book records today's findings in a committed baseline; a new finding fails, a fixed one is deleted from the baseline in the same change, and nothing is added to the baseline without a reason in the change description.
            check: scripts/check-structure --baseline .deep-modules.baseline
